messages:
maria_sales: Hey team — running a POC for Fintegral. They just reported a sudden spike of 429s on the /v1/generate route after a demo script run. Customer says it started when they ramped concurrent chats to 20. Can someone triage? tenant: fintegral-42, route: /v1/generate (model-redwood-8k).

alex_eng: Thanks Maria. Quick Qs: are these 429s all code 429_rate_limit or 429_quota? Any request IDs from the client logs? Also is this a per-route cap or global token budget?

maria_sales: The client pasted one error: `{"error":"429","type":"rate_limit","msg":"per-route cap exceeded"}`. No request id in that paste. They said they used the demo script that opens 20 websockets, each sending ~3 long prompts.

kai_oncall: This looks like per-route token burst exhaustion. Fintegral is on a shared trial plan so they have a small burst window and per-route ceiling to protect other tenants. Can you get me an example request-id or an approximate wall time? I can pull server logs.

maria_sales: I asked for request id; they gave this timestamp: 2026-03-21T18:14:02Z. No request id though.

sam_sre: I pulled the logs for tenant fintegral-42 around 2026-03-21T18:14. See snippet: ```
[18:13:59Z] tenant=fintegral-42 route=/v1/generate tokens=1120 burst_window=60s available_burst=0 -> 429 per-route-cap
[18:14:00Z] tenant=fintegral-42 route=/v1/generate tokens=900 burst_window=60s available_burst=0 -> 429 per-route-cap
[18:14:01Z] tenant=fintegral-42 route=/v1/generate tokens=1300 burst_window=60s available_burst=0 -> 429 per-route-cap
```

sam_sre: Bottom line: they consumed their burst budget in the 60s window. The token budget is per-route; streaming long prompts will quickly deplete it. Options: 1) Suggest client reduce concurrency or chunk prompts; 2) Temporarily increase their per-route burst (sales-approved short bump); 3) Configure demo to fall back to a smaller model when 429s occur.

alex_eng: For option 2 we can do a short-lived bump to per-route burst. Maria, do we have approval from sales for a temporary bump? If yes, I can run the change: update route_cap for tenant. CLI: ``redwood admin bump-burst --tenant fintegral-42 --route /v1/generate --add-burst 2500 --duration 30m``

maria_sales: I have verbal okay from Fintegral to try a short bump for the rest of their demo (30m). Customer asked for minimal disruption. Please proceed.

kai_oncall: I'm going to apply a conservative bump now and keep an eye on the dashboard. Pushing: ``/ops route update --tenant fintegral-42 --route '/v1/generate' --burst-add 2500 --ttl 30m`` -> operation id op_20260321_01

pagerduty-bot: Incident note created op_20260321_01: temporary per-route burst increase for fintegral-42. Oncall: kai_oncall.

sam_sre: After bump we saw this: ```
[18:14:40Z] tenant=fintegral-42 route=/v1/generate tokens=2200 available_burst=2500 -> 200 OK
[18:14:42Z] tenant=fintegral-42 route=/v1/generate tokens=1800 available_burst=1200 -> 200 OK
```

maria_sales: Customer confirmed the demo resumed and no more 429s reported. They also asked: how to avoid this in production?

alex_eng: Notes to hand off: - Recommend sizing guidance: expected tokens/session, concurrency. - Advise demo scripts to ramp gradually (5 -> 10 -> 20). - Offer a Dedicated plan or an increased reserved burst for production. - Add fallback to smaller model or partial responses when 429 observed.

sam_sre: I'll also add a short doc snippet we can share with Fintegral: `Best practice: cap concurrent chats to X for trial plans; add exponential backoff and a fallback model call on 429s; monitor token spend per route in Console > Usage > Per-route`.

maria_sales: Great — I'll send the note and close the loop with the customer. Thanks everyone for the quick help :thumbsup:

kai_oncall: Leaving a postmortem-lite for knowledge base: root cause = per-route burst exhausted by simultaneous long-stream requests; remediation = temporary burst bump + client ramp/fallback. I'll file a short KB entry.

maria_sales: Closing this thread.
